greeting: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Amen. We gather today in the presence of the Lord, seeking the grace to hear His word and the strength to live as His children.
penitential:
Lord Jesus, you call us to be one in your love: Lord, have mercy.
Lord Jesus, you clothe us in your own grace: Christ, have mercy.
Lord Jesus, you invite us to hear your word and observe it: Lord, have mercy.
psalm_response: The Lord remembers his covenant for ever.
homily:
There is a quiet, steady rhythm to the way a family moves through a day, a choreography of small habits that we rarely notice until they are interrupted. It might be the way someone always makes the coffee, or the sound of a voice calling out a greeting from the doorway, or the specific way two brothers might sit side-by-side, sharing a look or a laugh that needs no explanation. These are the threads of our lives, woven together into a tapestry of belonging. In the Gospel today, we find a woman in the crowd who is so moved by the presence of Jesus that she cries out, 'Blessed is the womb that carried you and the breasts at which you nursed.' She is looking at the physical, the tangible, the history of a mother and a son. She is reaching for the beauty of the human connection, the way a person is shaped by the love that birthed and nurtured them. It is a very human, very tender impulse. She sees the fruit of a life and she honors the root.

But Jesus, in His wisdom, gently shifts our gaze. He replies, 'Rather, blessed are those who hear the word of God and observe it.' He is not diminishing the human bond; He is expanding it. He is saying that the deepest, most enduring connection we have is not merely in the flesh, but in the spirit—in the shared obedience to the Father’s love. He is inviting us to see that we are not just defined by our earthly origins, but by our divine destination. We are being invited into a family that is much larger, much older, and much more permanent than any earthly house.

Think of the way Saint Paul describes this in our first reading to the Galatians. He says, 'For through faith you are all children of God in Christ Jesus.' He tells us that we have 'clothed' ourselves with Christ. Think of that image—clothing. When you put on a garment, it becomes part of you. It covers you, it warms you, it moves with you. Paul is saying that faith is not a theory; it is a wrapping. We are enveloped in the life of Christ. We are no longer defined by the old categories—Jew or Greek, slave or free, male or female. Those are the labels of the world, labels that try to divide us, to limit us, to keep us in boxes. But in Christ, those boundaries dissolve. We are all one. We are all heirs to a promise that does not end when the sun sets on our time here.

Benjamin Vo understood something of this, didn't he? He was a boy whose mind was always reaching for the horizon, always curious about the systems that hold the world together. Whether he was coding a game in his GitHub repository or looking up at the sky, tracing the flight path of a jet, he was a boy who lived with a sense of wonder. He was a boy who looked for the 'why' and the 'how' of things. But more than that, he was a boy who lived with a heart that was already tuned to that higher frequency of love. Remember the way he would giggle when he talked about his 'con chim airlines'? It wasn't just a fantasy about airplanes; it was a sign of a spirit that wanted to soar, that wanted to be part of something bigger, something that connected people across the vast distances of the earth.

Alan and Thao, I know that for these three months, the silence of your home has been a heavy companion. You remember the way Ben would come down the stairs, always the first to offer a 'Good morning, Dad.' You remember the way he would listen to your stories—those made-up, joking stories—with such rapt attention, as if they were the most important truths in the world. That was his gift to you. He was a boy who knew how to honor the people he loved by truly listening to them. And that listening was a form of prayer. It was a way of saying, 'You matter to me.' And because he lived that way, he was already living the Gospel. He was already hearing the word of God in the language of kindness.

There is a profound comfort in what Jesus says today. He does not say that we are blessed only if we are perfect, or only if we never stumble. He says we are blessed if we hear the word and observe it. It is a call to be present, to be awake, to be receptive. It is a call to realize that even in the midst of our sorrow, even in the middle of the 'midnight' of our grief, we are still being spoken to by God. His word is not silent. It is written in the love you still hold for Benjamin. It is written in the way Ryan carries the memory of his brother, in the way you continue to show up for each other, in the way you have chosen to let Ben’s love continue to flow through the 'Well of Love' in Vietnam. That well is a living prayer. It is a sign that the 'covenant' the Psalm speaks of—the covenant the Lord remembers forever—is being lived out through you.

I want to speak for a moment to the weight that can sometimes settle on the heart, the quiet questioning that happens when we are alone. Sometimes, we look back and we wonder if we could have done more, if we could have seen more, if we could have changed the path. I want to tell you, as clearly as I can: you were the parents Benjamin needed. You were his world, and he was yours. God does not look at your love and find it insufficient. He does not look at your past and find it faulty. You are not being asked to carry the weight of the past; you are being asked to walk into the future with the promise of the Resurrection as your light. Let that stone of self-reproach fall. It is not yours to carry. You are not being accused by God; you are being embraced by Him.

Ryan, you are a brother who knows the secret language of that love. You know that Ben is not gone; he has simply gone ahead to the place where all the 'con chim airlines' finally take flight. You are the one who carries the legacy of his curiosity, his kindness, and his smile. When you sit down to code, or when you look up at the clouds, know that you are not doing it alone. You are a family of four, and that bond is stronger than death. Keep being the boy who reaches out. Keep being the brother who knows that the most important things in life are not the things we possess, but the love we share. You are a witness to the fact that love is the only thing that actually lasts.

Think of the image of 'clothing' again. We have clothed ourselves in Christ. That means that when we are tired, He is our strength. When we are lonely, He is our companion. When we are confused, He is our clarity. The Gospel today is not a demand; it is an invitation to rest in the arms of the Father. It is an invitation to realize that Benjamin is already there, already resting, already waiting. He is in the 'Banquet of Heaven,' and he is watching over you with that same sweet, gentle smile you remember so well. That smile is not a memory; it is a promise. It is a sign that the joy he knew is the joy that is waiting for you.

We are here to be witnesses to that joy. We are here to keep the well of love flowing. Every time you are kind, every time you choose to forgive, every time you choose to hope in the face of despair, you are allowing his legacy to refresh the world. You are turning the soil of the earth so that the Kingdom can grow. You are the ones who are keeping his light burning in a world that so often forgets to look up. Do not be afraid of the silence, and do not be afraid of the ache. That ache is simply your love looking for a place to land. Let it land on the promise of the Resurrection. Let it land on the certainty that Benjamin is not in the past; he is in the future. He is at the destination, waiting for you to complete the journey.

So today, carry this away with you: you are never alone. You are a family that is being held by the same hands that hold the universe. When you see a bird in flight, or a plane climbing into the clouds, don't just see a machine or a creature; see a sign of the freedom that Benjamin now knows. See a sign of the promise that you are walking toward. Keep your eyes on the horizon. The journey is not over; it is simply continuing in a new, more glorious way. And one day, when the long road reaches the end, you will look up and see him waiting for you, and the joy will be beyond all reckoning.

Take this with you: you are a family of four, and that will never change. The geography of your life has shifted, but the bond of your love is eternal. Keep the 'Well of Love' flowing in his name. Keep the kindness moving. Keep the dream alive. And when you walk out those doors, look up at the sky. Remember that he is not in the dust. He is in the light. He is waiting for you, and he is watching over you with that same sweet, gentle smile that you remember so vividly. That smile is a sign. It is a sign that the harvest is coming, and that the One who started this good work in you will surely bring it to completion. You are loved without limit, and you are being held by the same hands that hold him. Amen.
petitions: For our dear Ben and all who have gone before us, that they may rest forever in the light of Christ’s peace, we pray to the Lord.
For all who grieve, that God may console them with the hope of the Resurrection and give them the strength to carry on in love, we pray to the Lord.
petition_call: For these intentions, we pray to the Lord.
spiritual_communion: My Jesus, I believe that You are present in the Most Holy Sacrament. I love You above all things, and I desire to receive You into my soul. Since I cannot at this moment receive You sacramentally, come at least spiritually into my heart. I embrace You as if You were already there and unite myself wholly to You. Never permit me to be separated from You. Amen.
closing: May the Lord bless you and keep you, and may His face shine upon you and give you peace. In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Amen.
standing_petitions: For a boy named Ben and all who have died, that they rest in the light of Christ.
For all who grieve, that God console them and give them hope.

readings.label: Reading 1
readings.text:
Brothers and sisters:
Scripture confined all things under the power of sin,
that through faith in Jesus Christ
the promise might be given to those who believe.Before faith came, we were held in custody under law,
confined for the faith that was to be revealed.
Consequently, the law was our disciplinarian for Christ,
that we might be justified by faith.
But now that faith has come, we are no longer under a disciplinarian.
For through faith you are all children of God in Christ Jesus.
For all of you who were baptized into Christ
have clothed yourselves with Christ.
There is neither Jew nor Greek,
there is neither slave nor free person,
there is not male and female;
for you are all one in Christ Jesus.
And if you belong to Christ, then you are Abraham’s descendants,
heirs according to the promise.

readings.label: Responsorial Psalm
readings.text:
R. (8a) The Lord remembers his covenant for ever.
or:
R. Alleluia.
Sing to him, sing his praise,
proclaim all his wondrous deeds.
Glory in his holy name;
rejoice, O hearts that seek the LORD!
R. The Lord remembers his covenant for ever.
or:
R. Alleluia.
Look to the LORD in his strength;
seek to serve him constantly.
Recall the wondrous deeds that he has wrought,
his portents, and the judgments he has uttered.
R. The Lord remembers his covenant for ever.
or:
R. Alleluia.
You descendants of Abraham, his servants,
sons of Jacob, his chosen ones!
He, the LORD, is our God;
throughout the earth his judgments prevail.
R. The Lord remembers his covenant for ever.
or:
R. Alleluia.

readings.label: Gospel
readings.text:
While Jesus was speaking,
a woman from the crowd called out and said to him,
“Blessed is the womb that carried you
and the breasts at which you nursed.”
He replied, “Rather, blessed are those
who hear the word of God and observe it.”

day: Saturday of the Twenty-seventh Week in Ordinary Time

pet_prayers.text: Ben ơi, trong giấc ngủ anh Huy đã thấy Ben về thăm anh, trao cho anh lời cầu nguyện để hai anh em mình lại được tìm thấy nhau. Xin Chúa thương nhậm lời Ben, cho Ben được hưởng ngàn thu bình an bên Chúa. Nếu có thể, xin Ben lại ghé thăm anh trong những giấc mơ tiếp theo nhé, dù chỉ là một lời chào hay một nụ cười thân thương như ngày nào.

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: Ben, my sweet boy, I miss you so much. Thank you for visiting me and Chú Chris last night. He told me he saw you flying a helicopter—so free, joyful, and strong up there. Down here, Mom and I are crying more and more each day. A piece of my heart feels completely dead without you, Ben. Please watch over us, pray for your mom, your brother Ryan, and me, and give us the strength to keep going. We love you forever

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: Today marks 100 days without you. Miss you a whole a lot Ben. Feel free to visit any time! See you around buddy! Love you!

Ben ơi, nay anh M đi xử lý hồ sơ ở Cam Ranh, đi ngang qua Cam Ranh Airport. Rồi cuộc nói chuyện về máy bay của Ben lại ùa về, nhớ nhiều kỷ niệm về Ben lắm ( anh M sẽ giữ kín kakaka). Quỷ nhỏ, tự nhiên nghĩ về mày buồn dễ sợ. Hãy đi đến những nơi mà Ben muốn nha và đừng quên là luôn nhớ về gia đình mình nhé, thương em trai nhiều. Giá như !!!!!!!!!

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: What happened my son? It's been 3 months since you left us. Missing you so much my whole body aches. Mom cries every day now... What are we going to do now Ben?  Please pray for us.

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text:
Hey Ben,

Rafael Rizzo and his little brother Ben really need your help right now. Please bless them with good health and give them the strength to get through this together. Please watch over Brandon and Flor's health, too.

I miss you a whole bunch. I know you're up in heaven watching over all of us. Whenever you're able to, stop by to visit, yeah? I love you and miss you so much!

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text:
Hey Ben - Miss you a whole bunch. Crying all day yesterday, i hope today will be better. Please guide our family through this grief... There's a 14 year old boy that just left earth on August 12... His name is Phero Aden Vo - look for him, maybe you guys can be friends...

Please pray for me and mom to have good health and strength.

I love and miss you Ben
